summary.text: Manny De Los Santos is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election in NY State Assembly District 72, running unopposed. Born in the Dominican Republic and raised in Northern Manhattan, he worked for 13 years as a social worker and community school director in New York City public schools before winning a February 2022 special election to the Assembly seat covering Washington Heights, Inwood and Marble Hill. He serves on the Banks, Education, Mental Health, Small Business, Social Services and Transportation committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in the Dominican Republic; according to his Assembly biography he was raised in Northern Manhattan and attended public schools. Lives in Washington Heights.
Earned a bachelor's degree in psychology and a master's degree in social work from the University at Albany (SUNY).
Worked for 13 years as a social worker and community school director in New York City public schools.

Served on the Neighborhood Advisory Board (NAB) and Manhattan Community Board 12 before his election; his Assembly biography says he coordinated voter registration and census drives and organized tenant, housing and immigration forums.
Ran in the September 9, 2014 Democratic primary for Assembly District 72, which Guillermo Linares won.

Won the February 15, 2022 special general election for Assembly District 72 as the Democratic candidate, defeating Nayma Silver-Matos (Uptown Rises) and Edwin De La Cruz (Republican); his predecessor was Carmen N. De La Rosa. He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Serves on the Assembly's Banks, Education, Mental Health, Small Business, Social Services and Transportation committees, and is a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus and the Task Force on New Americans.

According to his Assembly biography, he has worked on school funding and on legislation to reduce class sizes statewide that passed; the Assembly's news page reports that Governor Hochul signed his lithium-ion battery safety bill in July 2024.
